Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: A big work update (and a little Thanksgiving camera offer)

Quick update from the trenches! The trenches are now my own business, apparently.

It’s official: I’m going out on my own, and Fernhollow Photo is a real business now. I filed the LLC on my lunch break in the car outside Fred Meyer, which is not the glamorous founder origin story I pictured, but I did cry a little, so it had some drama.

I’ve been planning this in my head for two years, even if it still feels a little wild to say it out loud. Rosebud Lane closed at the end of October, and Marisol told me on October 6. I shot for her for four years, and I learned so much from her. She’s been generous and supportive through this whole transition, and six of my 2027 couples came to me through her referrals. Marisol, you deserve a very big thank-you for everything you taught me and for trusting me with those couples. I’m not going to pretend I’d be here without you.

The good news is I’m not starting from zero: I already have 14 weddings booked for 2027. Six came through Marisol, and eight found me on my own. That’s still a little hard to believe! My first booking that was completely mine was Dahlia and Ken for June 12 at Timberline. They found me through the Multnomah Falls couple photos I took for Marisol, and when their message came in, I did a tiny lap around the kitchen. Sam can confirm.

There’s a plan behind the excitement, too. I’ve got a marketplace health insurance plan lined up that starts January 1, and Jae will second shoot the bigger weddings with me, paid per wedding. (Dad: the insurance is sorted! I know you were going to ask. You can save the speech for a different occasion. Or at least keep it under five minutes.)

I’m excited, and yes, it’s scary. This is a big change, and I care a lot about doing right by the couples who’ve trusted me with their wedding days. But I didn’t decide this yesterday over a third cup of coffee. I’ve been thinking about it for a long time, working toward it, and getting the pieces in place. I’m ready to give Fernhollow a real try.

The name has a little family history in it. It comes from the fern hollow trail behind Grandma’s old place in Gresham, where I took my first real pictures with her Pentax. Grandma, this one’s for you. I still remember how it felt to look through that camera and realize I wanted to keep noticing things that way. Turns out I still do.

Sam made a cake that said FERNHOLOW because one of the Ls went missing, but it was delicious and we ate it anyway. The business is spelled right on the website, I promise.

So! At Thanksgiving, if anybody wants free family pictures, I’ll bring the camera. No pressure, no fancy setup, just a few photos of everyone together while we’re already in one place. (And if the cousins are feeling cooperative, I might even get one where everyone’s eyes are open.)

Love you all. I’m really excited to share this with you—and I’m grateful to have you cheering me on.
